text.title: Remote 1:1 Async Fallback: Failure Modes
text.summary: 6 known failure modes when running async-doc 1:1s as a fallback for cross-timezone PM and IC pairs. Each carries a detector (what to look for) and a repair (the corrective action).

failure-mode.description: Async by default: the pair has run async notes for months because it is cheaper for the PM's calendar; no synchronous call has happened, and the relationship has thinned to a form.
failure-mode.detector: More than 3 consecutive cycles with an async note and no synchronous call logged; notes lack a recorded infeasibility reason.
failure-mode.repair: Book a synchronous call before the next note and record the infeasibility reason per cycle (`r-async-only-when-sync-infeasible`).

failure-mode.description: Generic prompts: the note asks "anything to share?" and the IC answers "all good" for eight cycles while a blocker sits unreported.
failure-mode.detector: Any prompt under 10 characters or without a named ask (ticket id, decision owner, numeric scale); morale answers not on the pulse-survey axes; identical one-line replies across cycles.
failure-mode.repair: Restore the three named prompts with specific asks and the workload / autonomy / clarity scales (`r-three-named-prompts-fixed`).

failure-mode.description: Window in the PM's clock: the 48-hour window was posted Friday evening PM-time and counted over the IC's weekend or public holiday; the IC is marked unresponsive and escalated.
failure-mode.detector: `received_at` judged late using the PM's calendar; an unresponsive increment on a cycle overlapping the IC's weekend, holiday or formal leave.
failure-mode.repair: Recount the window in the IC's business hours, reset the wrongly incremented count, and mark leave-overlapping cycles paused (`r-response-window-in-ic-business-hours`, `r-formal-leave-pauses-the-cycle`).

failure-mode.description: Thumbs-up ack: the IC reports a stalled PR review and a pending decision, the PM acks with "thanks, noted" and an empty `next_actions`; the same blocker appears three cycles running.
failure-mode.detector: `ic_response.blockers` or `decisions_needed` non-empty while `pm_ack.next_actions` is empty; the same blocker text in consecutive cycles; `acked_at` more than 24 business hours after `received_at`.
failure-mode.repair: Ack within 24 business hours with owned, sprint-dated actions for every reported blocker or decision (`r-pm-ack-within-24h-with-owned-actions`).

failure-mode.description: Silent skip: the window expires, `escalation.action` stays `none`, the count never increments, and the PM posts the next note into the same silence; visibility of the IC is lost for a month.
failure-mode.detector: `received_at` null or past window with `action == none`; `unresponsive_count >= 2` with no manager escalation; a new note posted after two unanswered ones.
failure-mode.repair: Apply the ladder: count 1 offers a synchronous reschedule, count 2 escalates to the manager and blocks further async notes until sync contact (`r-escalation-ladder-reschedule-then-manager`).

failure-mode.description: Morale leak: per-IC morale scores from the private note end up in a team dashboard or a leadership deck with names; every subsequent answer from every IC becomes a 7.
failure-mode.detector: Named morale values in any artefact outside the pair's private channel; morale forwarded to the manager on escalation; sudden flattening of morale scores across the team.
failure-mode.repair: Remove named morale from shared artefacts; report only pair-level trend or an aggregate of 5+ ICs; send the manager the count and acked actions only (`r-private-channel-morale-never-aggregated-by-name`).
